title: 10 More or 10 Less
keyIdea: To find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number, change the tens digit by 1 and keep the ones digit the same: 10 more than 56 is 66, and 10 less is 46. On a hundred square, 10 more is the number straight below and 10 less is straight above, so there is no need to count on in ones.
familyTip: Point at a house number or a page number, like 34. Ask: what is 10 more? What is 10 less? Then check on a hundred square or with bundles of 10 straws.

visual.caption: Start at 52. Is each number 10 more, 10 less, or not a jump of 10? Drag each card, or tap it then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: jump a row on the hundred square, add and take tens, sort 10 more, 10 less and 1 more, then fix a piece of the square.

kid: A ten is a group of 10. To find 10 more, add one ten. To find 10 less, take one ten away.
Look at 56. It has 5 tens and 6 ones. Add a ten and you get 6 tens and 6 ones. That is 66.
Only the tens digit moves, by one. The ones digit stays the same. So 10 less than 56 is 46.
On a hundred square, 10 more is the box just under the number. 10 less is the box just above it. You do not need to count.
adult: Ages 6 to 7. CCSS 1.NBT.5: given a two-digit number, mentally find 10 more or 10 less without having to count, and explain the reasoning. In England, Year 2 place value (tens and ones) leads to the Year 3 aim to find 10 or 100 more or less than a given number.

The reason is place value. A two-digit number is tens and ones, so adding or removing one ten changes only the tens digit. On a hundred square each row holds 10 numbers, which puts 10 more directly below.

Common mistakes: counting on 10 single steps on fingers, which is slow and error-prone; giving 57 for 10 more than 56 because the ones digit was changed; going the wrong way on the square; and changing both digits.
In the lab your child jumps down rows, adds and removes ten rods, sorts 10 more, 10 less and 1 more cards, then rebuilds a cut-out piece of the hundred square.

practice.hint: Add one ten. Which digit counts the tens?
practice.explain: 56 has 5 tens. One more ten makes 6 tens, and the 6 ones stay. So it is 66. 57 is only 1 more.

practice.hint: Make the tens digit one bigger. Keep the ones digit.
practice.explain: {=a*10+b} has {a} tens and {b} ones. One more ten gives {=a+1} tens and {b} ones, which is {=a*10+b+10}.

practice.hint: Make the tens digit one smaller. Keep the ones digit.
practice.explain: {=a*10+b} has {a} tens. Take one ten away to leave {=a-1} tens and {b} ones, which is {=a*10+b-10}.

practice.prompt: You find 10 less than 73. Which digit changes?
practice.hint: 10 less takes away one ten, not one single.
practice.explain: 73 is 7 tens and 3 ones. Taking a ten leaves 6 tens and 3 ones: 63. Only the tens digit changed.

practice.prompt: On a hundred square, where is 10 more than 34?
practice.hint: Each row has 10 numbers. Which way do the numbers get bigger by 10?
practice.explain: Going down one row adds 10, so 44 sits just below 34. The box to the right is 35, only 1 more.

pool.hint: Take one ten from 8 tens. The 1 one stays.
pool.explain: 81 is 8 tens and 1 one. One ten less is 7 tens and 1 one: 71. 80 is only 1 less, and 91 is 10 more.

pool.prompt: Sam has {=a*10+b} stickers. He gets a pack of 10 more. How many now?
pool.hint: A pack of 10 is one more ten. Change the tens digit.
pool.explain: {=a*10+b} plus one ten is {=a+1} tens and {b} ones, so Sam has {=a*10+b+10} stickers.

pool.prompt: A shop has {=a*10+b} apples. It sells a bag of 10. How many are left?
pool.hint: Selling a bag of 10 is taking one ten away.
pool.explain: {=a*10+b} take away one ten is {=a-1} tens and {b} ones. That leaves {=a*10+b-10} apples.

pool.prompt: Mia says 10 more than 48 is 49. What did she do?
pool.hint: Look at which digit Mia changed.
pool.explain: 49 is 1 more: Mia changed the ones digit. 10 more changes the tens digit, so the answer is 58.

pool.prompt: Which number is just above 67 on a hundred square?
pool.hint: Going up one row takes 10 away.
pool.explain: One row up is 10 less, so 57 is above 67. 77 is below it, and 66 is to its left.

pool.hint: In a jump of 10 the ones digit stays the same.
pool.explain: 29 to 39 keeps 9 ones and adds a ten. 29 to 30 is 1 more, and 28 is 1 less.

pool.prompt: What is the quickest way to find 10 more than 45?
pool.hint: Think tens and ones. You do not need to count in ones.
pool.explain: 45 is 4 tens and 5 ones. One more ten makes 5 tens: 55. Counting fingers works but is slow, and 46 is only 1 more.

pool.hint: 9 tens and one more ten make 10 tens.
pool.explain: 10 tens is one hundred, so 10 more than 90 is 100. 91 is 1 more and 80 is 10 less.

pool.prompt: Put these in order, each one 10 more than the last.
pool.hint: Keep the 4 ones. Make the tens digit go up by 1 each time.
pool.explain: 14, 24, 34, 44: the ones digit stays 4 and the tens digit counts 1, 2, 3, 4.
